reviews.author: Areina B
reviews.text:
This was our second visit to Silver Falls State Park, and it was just as beautiful as we remembered — maybe even better this time around.

Our first visit was a few years ago during summer break. While it was gorgeous, it was also very crowded, and the waterfalls didn’t have nearly as much water flowing. This year, we decided to visit in May while the waterfalls were still full, and it was absolutely worth it.

We completed the full loop trail, about 8 miles total, and the hike felt very manageable with only mild elevation gain. The trail was pleasant and well-maintained, and seeing all 10 waterfalls along the route kept us motivated the entire way. Knowing another waterfall was coming within a mile made the hike feel exciting and rewarding.

The trail was definitely busy, but it never felt overwhelming. Most sections were wide enough for people to comfortably pass in both directions, and occasionally stopping for others was never a problem.

Every single waterfall was magnificent — powerful, full of water, and incredibly beautiful. We were lucky to have amazing weather too, which made the whole experience even better.

This park is truly one of Oregon’s treasures, and we’re already looking forward to coming back again next year.

reviews.author: Cynthia Mortensen
reviews.text:
Silver Falls State Park is a gem!! We stayed at the campground, which was clean, quiet and friendly. While at the park we hiked the Trail of Ten Falls along the Canyon, Winter and Rim Trails.    There were some closures due to fallen trees so we saw 7 out of the 10 falls plus several small falls. We did not expect the size and beauty of these falls! They are absolutely amazing!  Especially the falls you can walk behind! What a wonderful experience. We did not find the trails to be difficult. There are some stairs and elevation gains but they were not difficult and well maintained.
We went to the park on a Monday in March and it was not crowded. The falls had a large amount of water flowing this time of year, which was beautiful! This is not to be missed!

reviews.author: russ wheelhouse
reviews.text: Stayed two nights at a small cabin in the Smith Creek part of the state park. Very peaceful location for the cabins. Surrounded by big doug firs.  South Falls are about 10 minute drive away.  The full loop that takes you behind the falls is around 1.2 miles.  The trail has a drop of 300 feet.   Very beautiful area.

reviews.author: Rope G
reviews.text: This place is beautiful! Definitely one of the best campgrounds I've ever stayed at. The campsites are well maintained and lovely, with lush green foliage. The whole place is immaculate -- the staff do an excellent job of keeping everything tidy and clean. The people camping there seemed very friendly and respectful (nothing like the chaos and slovenliness we've seen at National Park campgrounds). We totally lucked out and got a site that was nicely separated from others, so it felt quite private and peaceful. Some of the sites (especially those on the insides of the loops) are less private. The campsites at the end of Loop A have a little road-noise from HWY 214, but it's infrequent enough not to be bothersome. The bathrooms were well maintained and clean. Hot showers are available free for campers. The park itself is also lovely; we enjoyed the 10-falls trail hike and also the mountain bike trails. There's also a nice bike path for those who need something a little more tame than mountain bike trails. I would definitely go there again.
reviews.title: Best Oregon hike in Spring

reviews.author: DN2021
reviews.text: Tent camped a couple nights in the campground and walked the Trail of Ten Falls one day. Some of the waterfalls along this trail are amazing. It was really neat to be able to walk behind a couple of them. This trail takes 4-6 hours so pack water and food if you do it. We were there on a weekday and the trail wasn't too crowded. I could see it having a lot of people on a holiday or weekend, though. Our campsite was large and under some very tall trees and had a small creek running behind it. The camp host also was very helpful. This state park is definitely one to visit.
reviews.title: Unbelievable waterfalls in a temperate rainforest

reviews.author: Topdown77027
reviews.text: Silver Falls State Park is amazing. Some bullet points. Good camping sites. Friendly Park rangers and campground hosts. Hikes are moderately challenging. Waterfalls are amazing. Close enough to Salem Oregon for an evening meal, activity and supplies. Spent three nights in the campground. Campfire wood available everyday. Good for tent camping. Pictures are a sample of the many falls. We broke up the long hike into two days. Equestrian trails are available as well.
reviews.title: 10 Falls Hike, Silver Lake, Oregon

reviews.author: Eric
reviews.text: I went here for my BD a couple years ago. We didn't camp here because my ex GF isn't into camping. We stayed at the Oregon Garden. This was my first time at both places. As for Silver Falls, since this is The Dyrt, it is a very nice campground. We were going to hike the upper fall loop but there was no parking. She's not a big hiker either. This was her second time. What was supposed to be a 2 mile hike turned into a 7 mile Trail of Ten Falls. She was a trooper and kept on going. I think she was terrified but think she liked the scenery.
